extracted.intended_audience: Authors and peer reviewers submitting original research to Nature and related Nature Research journals
extracted.subtask_description: Publisher policy and FAQ describing Nature's transparent peer review scheme: who it applies to, what is published, consent rules for authors and reviewers, redaction and transfer policies, and limitations of the published peer review file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and eligibility of scheme
rubrics_metrics.description: For all original research papers published in Nature authors can agree to the publication of a peer review file containing the reviewer comments to the authors and the author rebuttal letters. Transparent peer review will be offered to authors of newly submitted original research papers submitted on or after 1st February 2020. A similar initiative is currently being offered to authors of new submissions to [several Nature Research journals].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to original research papers and to newly submitted manuscripts from the stated start date; authors are offered the option at acceptance. Similar offerings exist across specified Nature-family journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author opt-in/opt-out consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are given the opportunity to opt out of this scheme at the point of acceptance. We will ask our authors if they would like to opt in/out at the point of acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors' explicit choice at acceptance determines whether their peer review file is published; authors may decline to participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer consent and acceptance implies permission
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers are informed of this initiative when invited to review and can decline to review the manuscript if they are not comfortable with their review being published. Acceptance to review is regarded as permission to release the reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must either decline the invitation if they do not want their report published, or by accepting, they are treated as consenting to publication of their report (subject to anonymity rules). Editors notify reviewers of the policy at invitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer anonymity and naming policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer names are not published. Unless reviewers sign the comments to the authors with their name, we will respect and maintain their full anonymity under all circumstances. Reviewers can request that their name be added to their comments at any point, up to and including receipt of a notification that the manuscript has been accepted in principle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default: anonymity preserved. Reviewers may choose to reveal their name by signing or by later requesting addition; requests allowed up to acceptance-in-principle notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of the published peer review file
rubrics_metrics.description: The peer review file will contain the full reviewer reports to authors and the author rebuttal letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The file comprises reviewer comments sent to authors and the authors' responses; editorial decision letters are not included (see separate item). The file is intended to give readers insight into expert recommendations that informed editorial decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing and redaction policy for peer review file
rubrics_metrics.description: The peer review file will not be edited except to redact confidential information or third party material. Authors will be able to suggest redaction of such material for the editor to review. All redactions when made will be noted in the peer review file, including any requested by the author and agreed by the editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only redactions for confidentiality or third-party material are permitted; authors may propose redactions but the editor reviews and decides. Every redaction is recorded in the file so readers see that material was removed and why (as noted). The journal may also withhold publication of reports in special cases (e.g., reports containing a lot of confidential clinical information).

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal discretion to withhold peer review reports in special cases
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal also reserves the right not to publish peer review reports in special cases, for example, where reports contain a lot of confidential clinical information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even with opt-in/consent, editors may decline to publish the peer review file when confidentiality or other concerns make publication inappropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy for manuscripts transferred between Nature journals
rubrics_metrics.description: If a manuscript is transferred from one Nature Research journal to another, reviewer reports are transferred as well. However, these reports and the author responses to them will not be included in the peer review file as they may have been submitted without consent to potential publication. If the same reviewers subsequently agree to review for the recipient Nature Research journal offering transparent peer review, only their reviewer reports for the recipient journal will be included in the published peer review file. Instances of transferred manuscripts that were previously peer reviewed will be marked up in the peer review file, without naming the other journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews obtained at a previous journal are generally excluded from the published file to avoid publishing reports given without consent; transferred-history is indicated in the file but the originating journal is not named.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations: what the peer review file does not capture
rubrics_metrics.description: The published peer review file will provide a reader with insight into expert recommendations that informed the editorial decisions. However, the richness and complexity of editorial debate and decisions will not be apparent as correspondence between authors and editors, reviewer comments made confidentially to editors, and internal discussions between editors will remain confidential. A paper might be published against the advice of a reviewer, if for example we receive confidential feedback from other reviewers that favours publication overall. These discussions might not always be fully captured in the peer review file, although we may add editorial explanations to some of the files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers should not expect the file to include confidential communications, editorial deliberations, or all influences on a decision; the file is a partial record and editors may add explanatory notes in some cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial decision letters not published
rubrics_metrics.description: No, Nature will not publish the editorial decision letters as part of the peer review file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit exclusion: editorial decision letters are kept confidential and are not part of the public peer review file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale and perceived benefits of transparent peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparent peer review is intended to make peer review more transparent and facilitate a deeper understanding of the research published. It creates a useful resource for students and early career researchers looking for information on how the peer review system operates. For reviewers, it has the benefit that if they wish to refer to or share one of their reviews they can do so easily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated goals: improve transparency, educate early-career researchers, and make it easier for reviewers to share their own reports if desired.
